title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 122 (Applicability of this Chapter to One Person Company)

content.overview: Section 122 excludes an OPC from section 98 and sections 100–111, provides a minute-book mechanism for the sole member's resolutions, and—where the OPC has only one director—provides a similar signed-and-dated minute-book mechanism for Board business.
content.glance: Section 122 excludes an OPC from section 98 and sections 100–111, provides a minute-book mechanism for the sole member's resolutions, and—where the OPC has only one director—provides a similar signed-and-dated minute-book mechanism for Board business.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 122 (Applicability of this Chapter to One Person Company). Subsection (1) excludes section 98 and sections 100 to 111 from application to an OPC. Under subsections (2) and (3), ordinary business normally transacted at an AGM and other business requiring an ordinary or special resolution may be dealt with by the member communicating the resolution to the company; it must be entered in the section 118 minute-book and signed and dated by the member, with the signature date deemed the meeting date for purposes of the Act. Under subsection (4), where the OPC has only one director, Board business may be dealt with by entering the director's resolution in the section 118 minute-book, signed and dated by the director; that date is deemed the Board-meeting date for purposes of the Act. Section 122 is not a blanket exemption from all other statutory duties. The topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Excluded provisions
sections.body: The provisions of section 98 and sections 100 to 111 (both inclusive) do not apply to a One Person Company.

sections.heading: Sole-member resolution and minutes
sections.body: Ordinary business identified by section 122(2), and business requiring an ordinary or special resolution at an AGM or other general meeting, may be handled by the member communicating the resolution to the company. The resolution must be entered in the minute-book required under section 118, signed and dated by the member; that date is deemed the meeting date for purposes of the Act.

sections.heading: Single-director Board resolution and minutes
sections.body: Where an OPC has only one director on its Board, business that would otherwise be transacted at a Board meeting may be handled by entering the director's resolution in the minute-book required under section 118, signed and dated by that director. That date is deemed the date of the Board meeting for purposes of the Act.

sections.heading: Other obligations
sections.body: Section 122 does not exempt an OPC from every provision of the Companies Act. Apply only the stated exclusions and the resolution/minute-book mechanisms in subsections (2)–(4).

provisions.title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 122 (Applicability to One Person Company)

examples.title: OPC member decision
examples.body: The sole member communicates a resolution to the company and records, signs and dates it in the section 118 minute-book, as provided by section 122.

examples.title: OPC with one director
examples.body: Where the OPC has only one director, that director records the Board decision in the section 118 minute-book and signs and dates the entry; the signature date is deemed the Board-meeting date under subsection (4).

hypotheticals.question: Does section 122 remove every statutory filing duty from an OPC?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Subsection (1) excludes only section 98 and sections 100–111. The resolution/minute-book mechanisms in subsections (2)–(4) are specific adaptations; other statutory obligations continue unless separately displaced.

hypotheticals.question: An OPC has only one director and must transact business that would ordinarily be dealt with at a Board meeting. What does section 122(4) require?
hypotheticals.analysis: The director's resolution must be entered in the minute-book required under section 118 and signed and dated by the director. The signature date is deemed the date of the Board meeting for purposes of the Act.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming section 122 removes every meeting-related and filing duty.
misconceptions.correction: Only section 98 and sections 100–111 are excluded by subsection (1); the other subsections establish specific resolution/minute-book mechanisms.

misconceptions.trap: Applying the sole-member procedure to Board business without checking subsection (4).
misconceptions.correction: Where an OPC has only one director, subsection (4) separately addresses Board business and requires the director's signed-and-dated minute-book entry.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How does section 122 modify general-meeting requirements for an OPC?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Sections 98 and 100–111 do not apply. In the circumstances specified, the member communicates the resolution to the company and records it in the minute book, signed and dated; the signature date is treated as the meeting date. Other obligations remain unless expressly excluded.

examTips: Quote the precise sections excluded by section 122(1).
Explain the communication, minute-book entry, signature and date requirements.
revisionPoints: Section 98 and sections 100–111 do not apply to an OPC.
Member resolutions under subsections (2)–(3) are entered in the section 118 minute-book and signed/dated by the member.
Where the OPC has one director, subsection (4) provides a separate signed-and-dated minute-book mechanism for Board business.
Section 122 is not a blanket exemption from the Act.
